subject: Re: Clarify billing model — per-token vs commit tiers for GreenField
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lpark@greenfield.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@greenfield.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing clarifications and vendor form

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — our engineering team liked the latency profile. Procurement has reviewed the materials and has two blocking items before we can issue a PO:

- GreenField requires a completed preferred vendor form (attached) and a clear PO line-item breakdown.
- Our finance team is uncomfortable with purely variable per-token billing for a production feature. They prefer committed tiers (monthly/quarterly) with known unit economics and clearly defined overage behavior.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: 1) accept a PO that references commit/tiers rather than raw per-token billing, and 2) provide an example cost table we can include in the Purchase Order?

If it helps, I can route your responses to procurement@greenfield.com and they can tell us the exact fields they need on the vendor form.

Best,
Lydia
Procurement Lead | GreenField Labs
(attachment: GreenField_Preferred_Vendor_Form.pdf)

From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <lpark@greenfield.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing clarifications and vendor form

Hi Lydia — great to hear the demo resonated. Short answers up front: yes, we can support commit tiers + overage pricing and accept a PO referencing those tiers.

I attached a simple pricing matrix that maps typical commit levels to blended per-token rates and overage rules. We can present that as an addendum to the PO or as part of an SOW. A couple details for your team to consider:

- Minimum commit options: Monthly tiers at $10k, $25k, $75k (USD) with step discounts (see attached matrix).
- Overage: Overage billed monthly at the agreed overage per-token rate; credits/true-ups can be part of a quarterly reconciliation.
- Billing entity: Redwood Inference, Inc. (we can send a W-9 and tax info once you confirm).

I'm attaching: pricing_matrix_Sept2026.xlsx and a completed copy of your preferred vendor form (I filled the contact and billing sections based on our records).

If procurement needs specific PO line-item language, loop them in and we will provide a PO template that references the tiered commit schedule and the HubSpot deal id.

Thanks — I'll also loop in Ben (sales ops) and Marissa (manager) to confirm the exact commit thresholds and internal approval for any credits.

Cheers,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
(attachment: pricing_matrix_Sept2026.xlsx)
(attachment: GreenField_Preferred_Vendor_Form_completed.pdf)

From: Lydia Park <lpark@greenfield.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, procurement@greenfield.com
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing clarifications and vendor form

Naomi — thanks for the quick turnaround and for filling the vendor form. A few follow-ups from procurement:

- The vendor form requires a PO line item that prefers a fixed monthly invoice amount tied to a service description and SKU. Can Redwood provide a single-line monthly amount per tier (we don't want multiple per-token line items on the PO).
- If you insist on per-token visibility, procurement wants it limited to an internal invoice appendix — not a line on the PO.
- They also asked for standard termination language and a statement on data handling for audit (SOC 2 attestation).

Procurement is concerned about variability vs budget predictability. Is Redwood willing to commit to a monthly spend floor per tier and then state overages as a separate invoice line (or better: as a reconciled credit)?

If you can email a one-page PO template and the SOC 2 certificate link, we can evaluate internally this week.

Best,
Lydia
Lydia Park | GreenField Labs
procurement@greenfield.com

From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <lpark@greenfield.com>, procurement@greenfield.com
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing clarifications and vendor form — proposed PO wording and compromise

Hi Lydia / Procurement — looping in Ben (Sales Ops), Marissa (Sales Manager) and Rishi (Legal) to get you a clean PO template and SOC2 link. Proposal below (short):

1) PO line item: Redwood Inference Managed Inference (Hosted API) — Monthly Tiered Commit — USD $[TIER_AMOUNT] — SKU: RI-HOST-TIER
   - The PO should include the monthly commit amount and effective date.
2) Appendix (internal/attachment to invoice): Per-token usage detail and overage calculation. This appendix is for internal reconciliation and will not change the PO face value.
3) Overage handling: Overage billed monthly at the agreed overage per-token rate and paid with net-30. Alternatively, we can do quarterly true-ups with a credit memo for predictable budgeting if you prefer.
4) Termination: 30 days written notice with pro-rated final invoice for commit + billed overages.
5) SOC2: public link — https://redwood.ai/soc2

We can produce a one-page PO template that contains the single-line monthly amount and references the appendix for usage detail. If procurement confirms the TIER_AMOUNT they expect for month 1, we will prepare a formal SOW/Schedule and send a DocuSign packet.

Attached: redline_SOW_v1.docx (sample SOW that maps tiers to SKUs).

Thanks — Ben/Marissa/Rishi, can you confirm we are comfortable with the quarterly true-up option as an alternative?

Regards,
Naomi
(attachment: redline_SOW_v1.docx)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing clarifications and vendor form — proposed PO wording and compromise

Looping internal owners:
- Ben: will produce the one-page PO template and tier-amount examples by EOD Monday.
- Marissa: will approve a capped credit allowance for quarterly reconciliations (propose up to 10% of monthly commit as an initial buffer).
- Rishi: please confirm termination language and whether the appendix approach is acceptable from a contract perspective.

Naomi — once we have the PO template, send it back to Lydia and procurement@greenfield.com. I suggest we offer the quarterly true-up option as the default and allow monthly overage billing if GreenField insists.

Thanks — Ben
